questions.text: The difference between the time taken by a train of length  240m crossing an electric pole with the speed of 40m/s and the same train crossing the y m platform is 1.5 seconds .Find the value of y.
questions.explanation:
Solution:

Length of the train = 240m

Speed of the train = 40m/s 

Length of the platform,

(240 + y)/40 - 240/40 = 1.5

(240 + y)/40 - 6 = 1.5

(240 + y)/40 = 7.5

(240 + y) = 300

y = 60m

Hence, option(3) is correct.

questions.text: The speed of 100 m long train is 50 km/h. It has to cross a platform of length 500 m. What is the time taken by the train to cross (2/5)th the length of the platform, if it increases its speed to double the present value?
questions.explanation:
10.8 seconds

Given:

The speed of the train = 50 km/h

The total length of the train = 100 m

The total length of the platform = 500 m.

Formula Used:

\(t= (l_p+ l_t)/v_t \);

where t  = time taken by the train to cross the platform,

\({l_p}\) = length of the platform,

\({l_t}\) = length of the train,

\({v_t}\) = velocity of the train.

Conversion of speed from km/h to m/s = velocity in km/h × (5/18)

Calculation:

(2/5)th the length of the platform = (2/5) × 500 = 200 m

Double the initial speed of the train = 2 × 50 km/h = 100 km/h

This speed in m/s = 100 ×  (5/18) = (250/9) m/s

So the total time to cover the required distance at the new speed = \(\frac{{200 + 100}}{{\left( {\frac{{250}}{9}} \right)}}\) seconds 

∴ The time taken by the train to cover (2/5)th the length of the platform at double its initial speed = 10.8 seconds

questions.text: Train A and Train B start at the same time one from Mumbai and other from Kerala at 80km/h and 90km/h respectively. Both the trains approach each other, when they meet. Train B travelled 150 km more than train A. Then, find the distance between Kerala and Mumbai.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Speed of A = 80 km/h

Speed of B = 90 km/h

Difference in their distance travelled = 150 km

Formula Used:

Distance = Speed × Time

Calculation:

Let x be the time after they meet

Distance travelled by train A = 80 × x = 80x

Distance travelled by train B = 90 × x = 90x

Now, difference between their distance travelled = 150 km

⇒ 90x – 80x = 150 km

⇒ x = 15 hours

After 15 hours they will meet

∴ the distance between these two places is (90 × 15 + 80 × 15) = 2550 km

questions.text: A train crosses a man standing near the track in 12 sec. After sometime, its speed is increased by 14.4 km/hr and it crosses another standing man in 10 sec. Later, its speed got reduced by 27 km/hr, and then in how much time will it cross a standing man?
questions.explanation:
Let the initial speed of the train be ‘s’ m/sec

As we know, Time taken to cross the man = length of train/speed of train

⇒ Length of train = 12s       - - - - (1)

When the speed is increased by 14.4 km/hr,

Speed of train = s + 14.4 × (5/18) = s + 4

⇒ Length of train = 10 × (s + 4) = 10s + 40       - - - - (2)

Equating (1) and (2) we get,

⇒ 12s = 10s + 40

⇒ s = 40/2 = 20 m/sec.

⇒ Speed of train = 20 + 4 = 24 m/sec.

⇒ Length of train = 12s = 12 × 20 = 240 m

Now when the speed is reduced by 27 km/hr,

Speed of train = 24 - 27 × (5/18) = 24 - 7.5 = 16.5 m/sec

∴ Time taken to cross a standing man = 240/16.5 = 14.5 sec

questions.text: Two trains crossed each other in 10 sec when the are running in opposite directions. The length of one of the trains is 510 m, while the ratio of their speed is 3 ∶ 2. Approximately in how many seconds the faster train will cross a platform which is half of its length if it's given the speed of the slower train is 129.6 km/hr and the longer train travels at a slower speed?
questions.explanation:
The ratio speed of trains are = 3 ∶ 2

∴ Let the speed of train be 3x and 2x respectively 

According to question,

2x = 129.6 km/hr

⇒ 2x = 129.6 × (5/18) m/s

⇒ 2x = 36 or x = 18

∴ 3x = 3 × 18 = 54 m/s

Now, let the length of second train be y m.

⇒ (510 + y)/(54 + 36) = 10 

⇒ 510 + y = 900 

⇒ y = 390 m

∴ Length of faster train = 390 m

Length of platform = 390/2 = 195m

∴ Time taken to cross the platform

⇒ (390 + 195)/54

⇒ 585/54 = 10.83 sec

∴ The faster train will cross a platform in 10.83 sec

questions.text: A train A starts from Raipur at 4 p.m. and reaches Bhilai at 5 p.m. while another train B starts from Bhilai at 4 p.m. and reaches Raipur at 5:30 p.m. The two trains will come across each other at what time?
questions.explanation:
Calculations:

Let the distance between Raipur and Bhilai be x km.

Time taken by A to cover x km = 1h

Time taken by B to cover x km = 3/2 h

∴ Speed of A = x km/h

∴ Speed of B = 2x/3 km/h

Let them meet y hours after 4 p.m. Then,

⇒ xy + 2xy/3 = x

⇒ y (1 + 2/3) = 1

⇒ y = 3/5 hours

⇒ 3/5 × 60

⇒ 36 minutes

So, the two trains meet at 4:36 p.m.

questions.text: The ratio of the speeds of a train and man is 9 ∶ 2. The train having a length of 450 metres crosses a post in 50 seconds. Calculate the time the train will take to cross the man while going in the same direction. (approx.)
questions.explanation:
Given:

The length of the train is 450 m

Time taken to cross-post is 50 seconds

The ratio of speed of train and man is 9 ∶ 2

Concept:

Distance covered in crossing a post or a man is equal to the length of the train.

Relative speed while going in the same direction is the difference of the speeds.

Formula:

Speed = distance/time

Time = distance/speed

Calculation:

Speed of train = 450/50 = 9 m/s

Speed of man = 90 × (2/9) = 2 m/s

Relative speed = 9 – 2 = 7 m/s

Time to cross the man = 450/7 = 64.28 seconds (approx.)

∴ Time taken by the train to cross the man is 64 seconds

questions.text: Two trains X and Y of length 150 metres and 200 metres are moving towards each other. Train X is moving at a speed of 54 km/h and train Y is moving at a speed of 20 m/s. find the time when both the trains cross each other.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Length of train X = 150 metres

Length of train Y = 200 metres

Speed of train X = 54km/h

Speed of train Y = 20 m/s

Formula used:

Time = Distance /Speed

Relative speed = Sum of their speed (When both are moving towards each other)

Calculation:

Speed of train X = 54 × (5/18)

⇒ 15 m/s

Speed of train Y = 20 m/s

Relative speed = (20 + 15) m/s

⇒ 35 m/s

Time = (150 + 200)/35

⇒ 350/35

⇒ 10 seconds

∴ Required time to cross each other is 10 seconds.

questions.text: The ratio of speed of Sujeet and Train is 3 : 11. They are running in opposite direction towards each other. Sujeet increases his speed 15% and then Sujeet and Train both meet after 2 hours. The distance travelled by both of them is 289 then find the initial speed of Sujeet.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Ratio of speed of Sujeet and Trains = 3 : 11

Total distance between Sujeet and Trains = 289

Time taken by both to meet each other = 2 hours

Formula used:

Speed = Distance/Time

Calculation:

Let the speed of Sujeet is 3x and speed of Train is 11x

According to question Sujeet increased his speed by 15% then Sujeet's speed become = 3x × (115/100)

⇒ 69x/20

Then (69x/20 + 11x) × 2 = 289

⇒ (69x + 220x)/10 = 289

⇒ 289x = 2890

⇒ x = 10

From here Speed of Sujeet = 3 × 10

∴ 30 km/h

questions.text: Two trains are travelling in the same direction at the speed of 62 km/hr and 80 km/hr respectively. The faster train passes a man sitting in the slower train in 10 seconds. Find out how much time will fast train take to cross a man who is walking on the platform at the speed of 10 km/hr in opposite direction of train?
questions.explanation:
Let Speed of both trains are Sf and Ss and speed of man is Sm

Sf – Ss = (Length of fast train)/Time

⇒ (80 – 62) × 5/18 = L/10

⇒ 18 × 5/18 = L/10

⇒ L = 50 m

Sf + Sm = (Length of fast train)/Time

⇒ (80 + 10) × 5/18 = 50/Time

⇒ 90 × 5/18 = 50/Time

⇒ 5 × 5 = 50/Time

∴ Time = 50/25 = 2 sec
